public_rationale: The 50% share cannot be reproduced from a consistent April inventory. CoreWeave's announcement establishes demand from Meta, so outside customers should not be treated as nonexistent. That does not establish how much construction serves the two labs. The nonpayment language describes a possible vulnerability; it is not a default forecast requiring an antecedent to occur.
limitations: Known contracts do not reveal the whole construction pipeline.
The hedged demand language and unquantified systemic-risk language cannot independently support a firm numerical verdict.

conditions: if OpenAI or Anthropic lacks money to pay

statement.excerpt: It’s also unclear whether the customer base for AI compute exists outside of OpenAI and Anthropic, whose demand accounts for 50% of AI data centers under construction, creating a massive systemic weakness if either of them lacks the money to pay.

our_interpretation: The surrounding GW discussion makes capacity share the ordinary reading of 50%, rather than a count of buildings.
I use the latest prepublication monthly snapshot: April 2026 through April 28. The post does not identify a measurement date.
Demand should be attributed to the ultimate compute customer, including capacity supplied through intermediaries, without double counting.
The nonpayment clause describes a vulnerability, not a forecast that either company will default. It does not condition the present-tense concentration claim.
The statement about other customers is hedged. Evidence of another customer is relevant context, but does not by itself disprove the 50% share.
criteria.support_condition: A consistent April inventory attributes approximately half of AI capacity under construction to OpenAI and Anthropic, with identifiable contractual exposure to those customers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable April inventory establishes a materially different combined capacity share. Evidence of other customers alone does not settle that share.
